Within the Morandi Museum housed at MAMbo, visitors encounter the serene world of Giorgio Morandi. With more than 250 works - paintings, sketches, etchings, and watercolors - this is the largest public collection dedicated to the artist anywhere in the world. Among them, *Fiori (Flowers, 1950)* and *Natura morta (Still Life)* reveal his quiet obsession with repetition, form, and color. His subtle studies of bottles, vases, and light stand in poetic contrast to MAMbo’s avant-garde energy, creating a powerful dialogue between tradition and modernity.

…

[MAMbo - Museo d'Arte Moderna di Bologna (Modern Art Gallery) > Practical Tips on Visiting MAMbo]

- **Best time to visit MAMbo:** Weekday mornings for quiet exploration or evenings during exhibition openings.
- **Entrance fee in Euros:** Around €6 for adults; free for Bologna Welcome Card holders.
- **Opening hours:** Usually open Tuesday to Sunday from 10 am to 7 pm; closed Mondays.
- **Official website:** 
- **How long to spend:** 1.5 to 2 hours for both MAMbo and the Morandi Museum.
- **Accessibility:** Fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers.
- **Facilities:** Café, bookshop, restrooms, and locker area available.
- **Photography tip:** The industrial architecture offers bold lines and natural light perfect for abstract shots.
- **Guided tours:** Available in English and Italian through the museum’s education program.
- **Nearby food options:** Trendy cafés and restaurants along Via Don Minzoni serve excellent local cuisine and aperitivi.

Hours and prices shift with the exhibition calendar, so check the official museum site before you set out, especially if you're going midweek when it may not open until the afternoon.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[MAMbo: Bologna's Museum of Modern Art > The building and the Manifattura delle Arti]

MAMbo sits in the former Forno del Pane, the old municipal bread bakery, which gives the galleries their big industrial volumes. The whole block has been reborn as the Manifattura delle Arti, Bologna's arts district. Within a couple of minutes you've got the Cineteca di Bologna film archive and cinema, university arts faculties, galleries and a stretch of restored canal. It makes an easy half-day if you pair the museum with a coffee and a film listing. There's a bookshop and a cafe-restaurant inside the museum itself.

[MAMbo: Bologna's Museum of Modern Art > Where it is and how to get there]

The museum is on Via Don Minzoni, northwest of the centre. From the main square it's about a 20 to 25 minute walk, mostly under porticoes, heading out past the canal district. On the way you can detour to the little window on Via Piella that frames Bologna's surviving canal, which is more or less on the route. Buses run up Via Marconi and Via Don Minzoni if you'd rather not walk.

[MAMbo: Bologna's Museum of Modern Art > Hours and tickets]

MAMbo is **closed on Mondays** and open the rest of the week, with later closing on the weekend and shorter afternoon-only hours midweek. Admission is modest, in the region of a few euro for the permanent collection with reduced rates for students, under-26s and over-65s, and separate or combined tickets when there's a temporary show on. Hours and prices shift with the exhibition calendar, so check the official museum site before you set out, especially if you're going midweek when it may not open until the afternoon."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.bolognawelcome.com/en/places/museums-and-art-galleries/mambo-modern-art-gallery-museum-","title":"MAMbo - Museo d'Arte Moderna di Bologna (Modern Art Gallery) - Bologna Welcome","description":"MAMbo is the Museum of Modern Art of Bologna and also comprises Casa Morandi and its Museum","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[MAMbo - Museo d'Arte Moderna di Bologna (Modern Art Gallery)]

The museum, located in an old bakery, offers a journey through the history of Italian art from the end of the Second World War to today, and is continually being renewed. Alongside the permanent collection, **extensive exhibitions** dedicated to important Italian and international artists are held. Since 2012, MAMbo has also temporarily hosted the Morandi Museum.

…

Among the works on display, one worthy of note is **Homage to the Hollywood Squares (featuring Bridget Riley)** by **Francesco Vezzoli** (2008). In this large square tapestry, the artist uses the medium, which has always featured in his work, to ironically rework references to Bridget Riley's Op Art and the textile art of Anni Albers.

In the Morandi Museum, visitors can also admire **Fiori** (Flowers, 1950), a topic covered by Morandi throughout the entire arc of his artistic research, gradually favouring dried or silk flowers to natural ones, and **Natura morta** (still life).

highlights:
[MAMbo - Museo d'Arte Moderna di Bologna (Modern Art Gallery) > Things to See and Do in MAMbo]

Within the Morandi Museum housed at MAMbo, visitors encounter the serene world of Giorgio Morandi. With more than 250 works - paintings, sketches, etchings, and watercolors - this is the largest public collection dedicated to the artist anywhere in the world. Among them, *Fiori (Flowers, 1950)* and *Natura morta (Still Life)* reveal his quiet obsession with repetition, form, and color. His subtle studies of bottles, vases, and light stand in poetic contrast to MAMbo’s avant-garde energy, creating a powerful dialogue between tradition and modernity.

…

- **Best time to visit MAMbo:** Weekday mornings for quiet exploration or evenings during exhibition openings.
- **Entrance fee in Euros:** Around €6 for adults; free for Bologna Welcome Card holders.
- **Opening hours:** Usually open Tuesday to Sunday from 10 am to 7 pm; closed Mondays.
- **Official website:** 
- **How long to spend:** 1.5 to 2 hours for both MAMbo and the Morandi Museum.
- **Accessibility:** Fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers.
- **Facilities:** Café, bookshop, restrooms, and locker area available.
- **Photography tip:** The industrial architecture offers bold lines and natural light perfect for abstract shots.
- **Guided tours:** Available in English and Italian through the museum’s education program.
- **Nearby food options:** Trendy cafés and restaurants along Via Don Minzoni serve excellent local cuisine and aperitivi.
